# IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program

The Mass General Brigham IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program is a national leader in the areas of clinical care and research for this recently recognized condition.

###### 617-726-7938

Call the IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program at 617-726-7938.

6177267938

style palette-deep-blue

### Addressing IgG4-RSD as a systemic disease

IgG4-related systemic disease (IgG4-RSD) links a number of inflammatory disorders that previously were considered unrelated. Various clinical manifestations of the condition can cause fibrosis (the formation of excessive connective tissue) in a growing list of organs and tissues.

Mass General Brigham is one of the only U.S. health systems to recognize and treat IgG4-RSD as a systemic (i.e. whole-body) disease that affects multiple organs and tissues. Our research on this emerging disease has led to several important milestones, including:

- Pioneering a new treatment (rituximab)
- Establishing IgG4-RSD's link with thoracic aortitis and with Riedel's thyroiditis
- Organizing the first international symposium on IgG4-RSD

### What to expect

Many patients are referred to us by a pathologist who suspects IgG4-RSD.

Your doctor will review your medical history, perform a physical examination and, because information about IgG4-RSD is so hard to find, educate you about the disease. If necessary, we may recommend blood tests or review your biopsy specimen with a Mass General Brigham pathologist to confirm a diagnosis.

For many patients, receiving the diagnosis of IgG4-RSD comes as a relief. The condition often causes organ swelling, which previously may have been mistaken for a malignant tumor. Some patients have even undergone unnecessary surgery for this reason.

If IgG4-RSD is diagnosed early, we can usually control the inflammation within organs and prevent further damage. In addition, our multispecialty expertise is essential in managing problems within organs that can result from damage associated with IgG4-RSD.

### Exploring a promising new treatment option

Treatment for IgG4-RSD traditionally has involved prednisone, a steroid medication. Prednisone has proven very effective in treating this condition but also leads to side effects such as weight gain, osteoporosis, high blood pressure and diabetes.

Mass General is hosting a clinical trial of rituximab, which to date has shown to be as effective as prednisone in IgG4-RSD but without the side effects. As a patient in our program, you will begin treatment for IgG4-RSD with two months of prednisone therapy. However, if symptoms subsequently return, you may be eligible to participate in the study of rituximab.

We typically see patients in our program monthly for the first three months of treatment and then every three months thereafter.

### About IgG4-related systemic disease

IgG4-related systemic disease (IgG4-RSD) typically affects multiple organs and tissues—most commonly the:

- Aorta tissue
- Kidneys
- Lacrimal glands (which produce tears)
- Lungs
- Pancreas
- Retroperitoneal tissue (in the abdominal area)
- Salivary glands

The condition causes fibrosis, in which the formation of excessive connective tissue prevents normal organ/tissue function. It may also lead to swelling that can be mistaken for tumors.

Particularly if diagnosed early, IgG4-RSD is highly treatable. Our program offers both traditional steroid therapy (prednisone) and, should that prove ineffective, a medication called rituximab that has shown great promise in treating the condition.

No matter what disease or condition you have, Mass General Brigham has specialists near you who can help.

###### 617-726-7938

Call the IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program at 617-726-7938.

6177267938

## Unlocking the mysteries of IgG4-RSD

A current Mass General Brigham clinical trial is studying the use of rituximab in patients with IgG4-RSD. Preliminary results have shown that rituximab therapy leads to the rapid decline of serum IgG4 levels and prompt clinical improvement. This trial is accepting new patients; please contact the Rheumatology Program for details on participating.

In the area of basic research, physicians from the Rheumatology Program were the first to report IgG4-RSD's link with thoracic aortitis and with Riedel's thyroiditis. Today, we are conducting several studies aimed at improving our understanding of the causes of IgG4-RSD. We plan to apply this knowledge in developing more-effective treatments for this condition.

## Understanding IgG4-Related Disease (IgG4-RD) 

IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a rare but serious inflammatory condition that can affect nearly every organ system in the body, including the pancreas, bile ducts, lungs, kidneys, and multiple glands. It can be challenging to diagnose and, if left untreated, can result in progressive and irreversible organ damage. There is also a major need to identify new treatments that can effectively treat this condition. 

Currently there are few centers of expertise in IgG4-RD in the country. University of Chicago is at the forefront of medicine as the sole clinical consortium for IgG4-RD in the Midwest. Our clinical consortium comprises experts from multiple specialties who are committed to providing accurate diagnoses, developing comprehensive treatment plans, and streamlining patients’ medical care for this disease. 

 The information below will give you answers to frequently asked questions about IgG4-RD and connect you with members of the UChicago IgG4-RD Clinical Consortium (IGGCC).

### What is IgG4-RD and what causes it?

IgG4-RD is a gradual, progressive condition characterized by activation of the body’s immune system, organ inflammation, and tissue fibrosis or scarring. It can trigger inflammation in any organ in the body and often times multiple organs at the same time. It is potentially autoimmune in character and can respond to medications that suppress the immune system.

### What type of symptoms are associated with IgG4-RD?

The symptoms vary depending on the extent and type of organ(s) involved. The symptoms can range from jaundice, abdominal pain, swollen glands, shortness of breath, vision changes, and/or urinary changes. Symptoms are generally non-specific for IgG4-RD, and so it is vital to work with a team with expertise in IgG4-RD to guide further diagnostic testing.

### How is IgG4-RD diagnosed? 

IgG4 diagnosis is typically made using a combination of diagnostic criteria that includes symptoms, imaging, blood tests, biopsies, and response to steroids. Careful review with experts skilled in the diagnosis of IgG4-RD is crucial.

### How is IgG4-RD treated?

Steroids are usually the first-line treatment, though patients may be at increased risk for relapse of their condition once steroids are stopped. There is emerging research on new drugs that can both treat and prevent recurrent inflammation in IgG4-RD.

### Who treats IgG4-RD?

Management is best with a multi-disciplinary team of rheumatologists, gastroenterologists, nephrologists, pathologists, and radiologists with respective expertise in IgG4-RD. Treatments should be tailored to each patient and is often based on type and extent of organ(s) involved.

### What is the UChicago IgG4-RD Clinical Consortium (IGGCC)?

The IGCCC is a team of experts with extensive experience spanning key specialties in the evaluation and management of IgG4-RD. We meet at clinical case conference to discuss new referrals, next steps for diagnostic testing, and recommendations with individualized treatment plans.

# IgG4 Related Disease Center

 Henry Ford Health is home to one of only a few centers in the country dedicated to treating immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) related disease (IgG4-RD). Our program provides comprehensive care for patients with this complex condition. 

 

### Learn More About IgG4-Related Disease Care

For years, Henry Ford Health has been a respected leader in IgG4-related disease care. Our multidisciplinary team combines their expertise and knowledge to provide a treatment plan that meets all your needs. Here, you’ll discover what sets our clinic apart.

## Why choose Henry Ford Health for IgG4-related disease care?

IgG4-related disease is an inflammatory condition that can affect nearly any organ. This condition occurs when your immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissues. Because IgG4-RD can mimic other conditions, diagnosis can be challenging. Our experts specialize in these diseases and can provide you with the answers — and treatment — you deserve.

The Henry Ford Health difference:

- Leading-edge expertise: We are home to one of the nation’s leading dedicated IgG4-related disease centers. Our experts established the program in 2013. Since then, we have cared for one of the largest populations with IgG4-related disease in the U.S., including patients with complex, multi-organ involvement. 
- Coordinated care: Our team of specialists meets regularly to discuss your care. This collaboration helps avoid duplicate tests and delivers a treatment plan that addresses every aspect of your health.
- Advanced treatments: As part of a major academic medical center with an active research program, we offer clinical trials for IgG4-related disease. These trials give you options when standard treatments haven't worked, and you have access to care not widely available elsewhere.

## Our multidisciplinary approach for IgG4-related disease

Henry Ford Health's IgG4-Related Disease Clinic includes a team of specialists who work together to provide coordinated care. A dedicated multidisciplinary team collaborates to confirm diagnoses and develop individualized treatment plans. Our team includes:

- Rheumatologists for coordination and management of your overall treatment plan
- Radiologists for diagnostic imaging and disease monitoring
- Pathologists for specialized tissue testing and IgG4 staining
- Surgical specialists for biopsies and management of organ-specific complications

Depending on your needs, you may also receive care from:

- Digestive specialists including gastroenterologists for digestive system diseases and hepatologists for liver and biliary disease
- Endocrinologists for endocrine and hormonal disorders 
- Neurologists for disorders of the brain and nervous system disease
- Ophthalmologist s for eye and orbital disease
- Otolaryngologists (ENT) for enlarged salivary glands and sinus problems
- Pulmonologists for lung and respiratory complications
- Urinary specialists including urologists for urinary tract and genitourinary disease and nephrologists for kidney disease and autoimmune pancreatitis

Below, you’ll learn more about treatment for IgG4-related disease and our approach at Henry Ford Health.

## Diagnosing IgG4-related disease

IgG4-related disease can be challenging to diagnose. Symptoms can look like other conditions, such as infections or cancer. Our team provides comprehensive testing for the most accurate results, which may include: 

- Clinical exam

We may perform a physical exam and review your personal and family medical history.
- Lab tests

Blood tests can measure IgG4 levels and provide information about your organ function. Elevated IgG4 levels alone don’t mean you have the disease, so our specialists also perform other tests to confirm the diagnosis.
- Imaging

Our team uses CT scans, MRI and PET scans to identify affected organs and the extent of disease. Radiologists with specific expertise in recognizing the imaging patterns of IgG4-related disease review your image results.
- Pathology

When needed, our pathologists perform specialized IgG4 immunostaining and expert review. Accurately interpreting these tissue samples is essential to diagnosis. Our team has extensive experience evaluating samples from patients with suspected IgG4-related disease.
- Multidisciplinary review

We hold multidisciplinary meetings where multiple experts review findings together. This team of specialists is highly experienced in accurate IgG4-related disease diagnosis and optimal treatment planning.

## Treatment for IgG4-related disease

Led by IgG4-related disease specialists, our clinic provides patients with the most advanced treatments for multi-organ autoimmune disease, including autoimmune pancreatitis. We base your treatment plan on which organs are affected, disease severity and other factors. Your care may include:

- Corticosteroids

These medications reduce inflammation and prevent organ damage. Our specialists may start with these medications and evaluate your progress. If they don’t provide positive results, we offer additional options based on your health needs.
- Immunosuppressive medications

These medications include biologics (medications that block certain parts of your immune system) and targeted therapies, which focus on specific parts of your immune system. These therapies can calm your immune response and help prevent organ damage. We carefully monitor you for side effects and treatment efficacy.
- Clinical trials

Our physicians participate in national and international research efforts focused on improving the diagnosis and treatment of IgG4-related disease. Eligible patients may have access to clinical trials and emerging therapies only available at a limited number of specialized centers.
- Organ-specific care

Depending on which organs are affected, you may receive additional treatments from our specialists. For example, you may see an ophthalmologist for eye problems, a pulmonologist for breathing issues and a rheumatologist for care coordination.

## FAQs for IgG4-related disease

Common questions about IgG4-related disease include:

- What is IgG4-related disease?

IgG4-related disease is a rare chronic condition where your immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissues. Your body produces too many special proteins called IgG4 antibodies, which cause swelling, fibrosis (scarring) and damage in one or more of your organs. The disease isn’t contagious, and parents can’t pass it on to their children.
- What are the symptoms of IgG4-related disease?

Because IgG4-related disease can affect many organs, it can have many different symptoms. A lot of people first notice painless swelling in their salivary glands, lymph nodes or around the eyes. You might have stomach pain, yellowing skin, shortness of breath or fatigue. Some people also have kidney problems, weight loss, low-grade fevers or just feel unwell.
- Why is it important to see a specialist for IgG4-related disease?

IgG4-related disease is challenging to diagnose because it mimics many other conditions, like cancer. Specialists understand how to diagnose the condition and know which medications may work best for you. At Henry Ford Health, our experts also identify any organ damage early and coordinate your care across multiple specialties to cover all your needs
- What makes Henry Ford Health a leader in IgG4-related disease?

Since 2013, Henry Ford Health has served as a regional and national referral center for patients with suspected or confirmed IgG4-related disease. Our physicians contribute to clinical research, educational initiatives, and international collaborations focused on improving diagnosis and treatment of this rare condition. Patients travel from throughout Michigan and across the country to seek care from our multidisciplinary team.

results.text:
# IgG4-Related Disease (IgG4-RD)

IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is an immune-mediated condition, meaning that it involves the occurrence of disease in organs as the result of an abnormally regulated immune system. The classic IgG4-RD patient is a middle-aged to elderly individual – more likely to be male than female. In rare cases, the disease also affects children. Some patients with IgG4-RD have disease in only one organ. Others, however, have diseases that affect multiple organs at the same time. It is not unusual for disease to affect anywhere between two to six organs. The following organs are often involved in IgG4-RD: (1) meninges, (2) orbits, (3) lacrimal glands, (4) major salivary glands, (5) thyroid gland, (6) lungs, (7) aorta, (9) kidneys (10) pancreas, (11) bile ducts.

### What Are the Signs/Symptoms

Many patients with IgG4-RD may have no signs or symptoms for months or even years before the diagnosis is made, which can cause organ damage even while the patient is feeling well, long before he or she comes to medical attention. Because of the many organs that IgG4-RD can affect, the disease can exist in multiple ways associated with many symptoms. IgG4-RD can often appear as a mass that mimics cancer. Other common symptoms include fatigue, weight loss, headaches, dysfunction of the cranial nerves, bulging of one or both eyes, bulges on the sides of the face or below the chin, inflammatory tissue in the thyroid, large vessel vasculitis (inflammation in the blood vessel wall), shortness of breath, blockage of urine flow from the kidney, enlarged kidneys, abdominal pain and painless jaundice (yellow tint to the skin or eyes).

### What Are Common Treatments?

If diagnosed before serious organ damage has occurred, IgG4-RD typically responds well to treatment, but chronic therapy is necessary. Glucocorticoids are typically viewed as the initial treatment of IgG4-RD. Although nearly all patients with IgG4-RD respond to glucocorticoids, approximately 40% of those fail to achieve complete remission or relapse within one year. The disease often recurs after glucocorticoids are stopped. Rituximab, however, is frequently an excellent treatment for IgG4- RD, and it is not typically associated with many of the adverse effects linked to glucocorticoids.

### Living with IgG4-RD

Patients with IgG4-RD need to have close follow-ups with physicians who are knowledgeable about IgG4-RD. They also need to broaden their own knowledge of this condition and be aware of the symptoms and complications that can result from disease in the organs. Because of the organ damage IgG4-RD, it is important to seek medical attention for symptoms early and begin treatment.

# Inflammatory Disease Genetics Program 

 212-598-2374 

At NYU Langone’s Inflammatory Disease Genetics Program, the geneticists, rheumatologists, and certified genetic counselors on our team care for adults and children with autoinflammatory conditions whose symptoms are severe or whose cause is unknown.

We use both genetic testing and research-based analysis to identify the underlying genetic causes of these conditions. Using this information, we work to provide the most-advanced targeted therapies, counseling about how the condition may develop and change over time, as well as risk assessment for other family members.

Our team specializes in autoinflammatory conditions in which inflammation recurs without clear signs of infection, autoimmune disease, or cancer, including the following:

- VEXAS syndrome, a rare but serious condition that can cause unexplained symptoms throughout the body, such as fever and fatigue, painful skin rashes, pain and swelling of the ears and nose, coughing or shortness of breath, and vasculitis. Learn more about how we care for people with VEXAS syndrome.
- periodic fever syndromes, which are conditions characterized by recurring fevers not caused by an infection
- severe, unexplained inflammation that causes symptoms in the bone marrow, lungs, cartilage, or skin

Our experts evaluate the underlying genetic cause of autoimmune diseases with the goal of improving care for children and adults
